subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Should this report be closed as unsupported by the current gateway authorization model, or should the reporter first provide a current-main boundary-crossing WebSocket PoC?
rationale: The source strongly contradicts the proposed sequence-ID attack, but the protected security label reserves final vulnerability disposition for an authorized security owner.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that event sequence values are non-authoritative ordering metadata and close unless a current boundary-crossing PoC is supplied.

options.title: Request a focused PoC
options.body: Keep the report pending while requesting raw redacted frames showing an unauthenticated or under-scoped connection injecting an accepted RPC.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence values are non-authoritative ordering metadata and close unless a current boundary-crossing PoC is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history signal is gateway authentication, pairing, and forwarded-client boundary hardening.
